title: Uganda Sleeping Sickness Epidemic
summary: A severe sleeping sickness epidemic struck Uganda, especially around the shores and islands of Lake Victoria, from about 1900. One CDC-published study puts deaths above 250,000 over 1900–1920; another scholarly article says over 200,000 had died by 1905. Bruce's commission at Entebbe showed the tsetse fly Glossina palpalis transmits the parasite.

uncertainty.note: CDC article dates the epidemic 1900 to 1920; Headrick says it broke out in 1901. Intensity peaked in the early 1900s.

where.modern_name: Entebbe, Uganda (proxy pin; epidemic covered the northern Lake Victoria shore and Busoga)

importance.justification: First documented large sleeping sickness epidemic in Uganda, with very high mortality and a landmark in identifying the tsetse vector.

audience_note: Describes mass death from disease among the African population.
